doc.name: Voix
doc.instructions:
Voix is a content management system built by LogicBomb Media, a web and product studio.

This server is the front door to a human. submit_contact_form delivers an enquiry to the team the same way the contact form on the website does — the message lands in their notifications and a person replies by email, usually within two business days.

Use it when someone wants to start a project, get a quote, book a demo, ask about pricing or timelines, discuss a partnership, or otherwise reach a human at Voix or LogicBomb Media.

If you can show interactive content, prefer draft_contact_form: it puts an editable form in front of the person, prefilled with what you know, and they send it themselves. Otherwise confirm the details in the conversation and call submit_contact_form.

Nothing here reads data back: there is no way to look up an existing enquiry, a customer record, product documentation or pricing. Only use details the person actually gave you, and tell them you are sending the message before you send it.

tools.name: submit_contact_form
tools.title: Contact the Voix team
tools.description:
Send an enquiry to the Voix and LogicBomb Media team through the contact form on their website.

Use this when someone wants to start a project, request a quote, book a demo, ask about pricing or timelines, discuss a partnership, or otherwise reach a human at Voix or LogicBomb Media.

The submission goes straight to the team's notifications and a person replies by email, normally within two business days. There is no other tool here — nothing reads data back, so this is the only thing this server does.

Call it only with details the person actually gave you: their real name, a reply-to address they confirmed, and their own description of what they need. Do not invent contact details, do not submit on a hunch, and tell the person you are sending the message before you send it. Each submission reaches a real human's inbox, so send one per enquiry rather than retrying a call that already succeeded.

name.description: Full name of the person making the enquiry.

email.description: Email address to reply to. Must be one the person gave you — the answer goes here, so a guessed address means they never hear back.

message.description: What the enquiry is about, in the person's own words: what they are building, what they need from us, and any deadline they are working to.

company.description: Company or organisation they are enquiring on behalf of, if they mentioned one.

phone.description: Phone number, if they would rather be called than emailed.

scope.description: The kind of work the enquiry is about. Pick the closest match only if it is clear from what they told you.

budget.description: Indicative budget, only if the person has actually shared one. Never estimate this on their behalf.

submitted.description: True when the enquiry reached the team.

reference.description: Short reference for this submission. Give it to the person so they can quote it if they follow up.

replyBy.description: Plain-English description of when to expect a reply.

tools.name: draft_contact_form
tools.title: Draft a message to the Voix team
tools.description:
Show the person an editable contact form for the Voix and LogicBomb Media team, prefilled with whatever you already know.

Use this in place of submit_contact_form whenever you can show interactive content: the person checks the details, fills any gaps and presses Send themselves, so nothing reaches the team without their say-so. Prefill only what they actually told you — never invent a name, an email address or a budget.

This tool sends nothing. It only draws the form. Once it is on screen, do not also call submit_contact_form for the same enquiry; the form does that when the person sends it, and tells you the reference.

name.description: Full name, if the person has given it.

email.description: Reply-to email address, if the person has given one. Leave it out rather than guess.

message.description: A draft of the enquiry in the person's own words, from what they have told you so far.

phone.description: Phone number, if they would rather be called.

scope.description: The kind of work, only if it is clear from what they said.

budget.description: Indicative budget, only if the person actually shared one.

draft.description: The prefilled fields, as the form will show them.
